subject: Known issues with expm1 and perm?

messages.author: 3f1b57241ff195d2
messages.subject: Known issues with expm1 and perm?
parts:
Hi

I wonder whether there are known issues or something that one needs to be particularly careful about, when using the following two calls in the c++ likelihood function: 

1. expm1 from CppAD (https://www.coin-or.org/CppAD/Doc/expm1.htm) 
2. perm from tmbutils (https://kaskr.github.io/adcomp/structtmbutils_1_1array.html)

These two functions are central in my likelihood definition, and I am running into some convergence issues, that I suspect might be to any of these somewhat unusual functions. The compilation and evaluation of the function itself are both successful.

Any input on this is highly appreciated!

messages.author: 02e03030784aa6a7
messages.subject: Re: Known issues with expm1 and perm?
parts:
I am using the TMB version expm():  https://kaskr.github.io/adcomp/group__matrix__functions.html#gac09966696ad9685dc8047d6c582bc0ae a little,
and I have not run into problems. However, I believe that there are many alternative algorithms for the matrix exponential, maybe indicating
that there can be problems in certain ranges.

messages.author: 3f1b57241ff195d2
messages.subject: Re: Known issues with expm1 and perm?
parts:
Thanks for the input. Note, however, that I am referring to the function expm1() (exp minus one), which is just evaluating exp(x)-1 in a stable fashion for x close to 0.

I don't see how the behavior of expm() is relevant. Did you just misread, or I am missing something? 

Could it be that, for some reason, automatic differentiation with respect to functions involving expm1() and perm() is problematic?

- Martin
